Hi, this is a known issue. I mainly added this as a safeguard to prevent users from getting an unpleasant surprise, since some renders can take 48+ hours and burn through all their tokens. It's more of a warning than a proper fix for now, but definitely something that needs improvement.

Thanks for the idea! Not at the moment an Anatomy figure is a drawing rather than a 3D model. The kit builds each part from real 3D shapes, then projects and shades them into an isometric SVG, and only that drawing is saved, so there’s no mesh to hand to other tools.

An export is possible in principle. Every part starts as a 3D solid, so the kit could write those out as glTF/GLB meshes, with 3D-mode groups as nodes so turning parts still turn. But it would be the geometry only, none of the line work, shading, text, shaders or interactivity that make a figure look like an Anatomy figure.

What would you use the GLB for blender, a three.js scene, AR, something else? That would tell us whether plain geometry is useful enough to build. Leaving this open as a feature request.

Thank you, this is a great proposal and it fits what Anatomy is for, the explanation one level down, sharing the parent’s model. The rules you sketched (the child owns its model, only parts that hide a real idea open, and the zoom stays in the same world) are the right ones.

It’s a big step, since each level is a full figure and the zoom between levels is new work, so I’d like to do it the way the skill has grown so far build one reference example by hand first (your computer → CPU → ALU is perfect), learn the rules from it, write them into references/depth.md, and only then add levels=. Keeping this open as the plan for that.

Quick take on each point:

**1. Canvas painter / shift fast-path:** Yes, that's the direction. The plan is to keep the engine as the source of truth (geometry, depth order, labels, audits) and make the painter swappable: SVG stays the default, canvas/WebGL becomes opt-in for dense scenes. They're not folded into `turn.mjs` yet because they still need to pass the full `turn-check.mjs` suite reliably. I'd rather take it slow on this one, so no PR needed yet.

**2. Zoom levels (#51):** Still want to hand-build the computer → CPU → ALU figure first. I'm leaning toward camera/viewBox interpolation in SVG so the transitions stay auditable, with stage zoom as a possible fast path for the canvas painter later. Not settled though, happy to hear arguments.

**3. Parallel `turn-audit.mjs` with `worker_threads`:** Yes please. The audit outlasting agent timeouts is a real pain point. Opt-in first (e.g. a `--workers` flag), and results must be identical to the single-threaded run. If you can show that on a few existing figures, I'd happily merge.

**4. React/Next.js harness:** Interested, as long as it stays an opt-in script and doesn't add dependencies to the kit itself. Feel free to open a draft PR.

**5. MiniMax Code in `publish.mjs` + session parsers:** Yes, adding MiniMax to the list is an easy one. For session parsers, go ahead for agents whose log format is stable; one parser per PR is easiest to review.

If you want to start somewhere, #3 and #5 are the ones I'd merge fastest. Thanks again!

To follow up on your caveat about live Antigravity transcripts: we ran `scripts/session.mjs` directly against real live Antigravity session logs in `~/.gemini/antigravity/brain/<conversation-id>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl` (and `transcript_full.jsonl`).

1. **Live schema match:** Real Antigravity logs emit:
   - `USER_INPUT` with `source: "USER_EXPLICIT"`, `created_at` (ISO 8601 UTC), and `content` wrapped in `<USER_REQUEST>...</USER_REQUEST>` + `<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>`.
   - `PLANNER_RESPONSE` with `step_index`, `created_at`, `input_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, and `output_tokens`.
   - `GENERIC` for `invoke_subagent` tool responses with `Created At: ...\nCompleted At: ...\nCreated the following subagents:\n{\n  "conversationId": "..."`.
2. **Hardening from live testing (`2c9f...` / latest commit):**
   - `subagentIds` now reads `transcript_full.jsonl` when present alongside `transcript.jsonl` (in case a step spawning many subagents had `truncated_fields: ["content"]` in the compact log) and anchors `"Created the following subagents:"` to the tool response header so `run_command` or file-read steps that happen to mention that string in their output are never mistaken for spawned subagents.
   - `measure` now uses `head ? asks.find(...) : null` before `??` so calling `fromThisSession` or `measure` without a `prompt` falls back cleanly to `/\/anatomy\b|\banatomy\b/i` instead of short-circuiting on `""`.

- **Item 5 — #96 (`publish.mjs` + `session.mjs`):** Adds `"MiniMax Code"` to the `--agent` whitelist (resolving #88) and adds the Antigravity session parser (`~/.gemini/antigravity/brain/<id>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl` + spawned subagents, excluding `cache_read_tokens`). Verified against both unit fixtures and live Antigravity transcripts.
- **Item 3 — #97 (`kit/turn-audit.mjs` `--workers`):** Adds opt-in `node:worker_threads` parallelism (`--workers` / `--workers=N` / `workers: true | N`) with synchronous `Atomics.wait` + `MessageChannel` coordination and 100% single-threaded result parity (`diff -u` identical across all checks, ordering, and reports):

  | Command | Single-threaded | `--workers` (10 cores) | Speedup | Report diff (excl. elapsed s) |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---|
  | `node examples/turning-dial/build.mjs --light --audit` (full) | 452.24 s | 115.48 s | **3.92×** | 0 lines |
  | `node examples/turning-dial/build.mjs --light --audit --quick` | 43.01 s | 13.51 s | **3.18×** | 0 lines |
  | `node examples/turning-dial/stress.mjs --light --audit --quick` | 70.07 s | 25.42 s | **2.76×** | 0 lines |

- **Item 4 — #98 (`scripts/react-page.mjs`):** Adds an opt-in standalone page builder for React/Next.js figures (`node scripts/react-page.mjs <figure-dir | file.tsx> [--light] [--out]`) with zero dependencies added to `kit/`. Bundles and runs `renderToString` + `hydrateRoot` using `react`, `react-dom`, and `esbuild` from `NODE_PATH` or project `node_modules`, resolves `@/` / `~/` / `tsconfig.json` `paths` (falling back to `kit/` for `@/components/iso/…`), and inspects `"use client"` boundaries during SSR to flag missing root `key`s on element props and nested client components. Verified on `examples/test-rig` and `examples/spot-plate` in both themes with `capture.mjs` and `drive.mjs`.

Following up on @wheresryan22's note in #85 about **SVG camera/`viewBox` interpolation vs. stage zoom** for the `computer → CPU → ALU` reference figure:

Because `fitProjection` is orthographic (`x' = ox + k·u`, `y' = oy + k·v`), two projections `P_parent` and `P_child` that share the same `(azimuth, elevation)` differ **only by a 2D similarity transform** in viewBox space (`s = P_child.k / P_parent.k`, plus a translation `[ox, oy]`).

That gives camera/`viewBox` interpolation with per-level `fitProjection` (`P_0, P_1, P_2`) four concrete advantages over CSS/stage zoom:

1. **Per-level `audit.mjs` and `lines.mjs` without grid blowup or tolerance drift:**
   - `lines.mjs` checks attachments against a fixed `1`–`2` viewBox-px tolerance, and `A.settle` / `overlapsOf` rasterizes at `P`'s scale.
   - If `computer` ($1\times$), `CPU` ($\sim 4\times$), and `ALU` ($\sim 16\times$) were all emitted into a single `P_0` coordinate space, level-2 details would be $1/16\text{th}$ of a viewBox pixel (breaking `lines.mjs` tolerances and requiring a $256\times$ denser ray-cast grid in `audit.mjs`).
   - Authoring each level `L` against its own `P_L = fitProjection(bounds_L, width, height, { azimuth, elevation })` keeps every level's viewBox `width × height` at $1\times$ scale. Each level runs its own `R_L = A.recorder(P_L)` and `lines.mjs` check at native resolution, while the shared boundary solid (e.g. CPU socket / package frame) is recorded in both `R_L` and `R_{L+1}` so `supports` and `terminals` are proved across the level boundary.

2. **Exact placement & crisp stroke widths across the transition:**
   - Since `P_child(p) = s · (P_parent(p) - [ox, oy])`, the child level's `[0..W, 0..H]` drawing sits inside the parent's SVG at `<g transform="translate(ox, oy) scale(1/s)">`.
   - As the parent cover lifts (`translateAlong`) and `<svg viewBox>` interpolates from `[0, 0, W, H]` to `[ox, oy, W/s, H/s]`, the child `<g>` lands at exact `1:1` viewBox scale when `t = 1`—so its `iso-outline`, `iso-crease`, and `iso-line` strokes have the exact same pixel weight at rest as the parent's did at `t = 0`.

3. **Seamless WebGL registration (`kit/gl.mjs`) during zoom:**
   - In `glCamera(P)`, `uCam = [ca, sa, se, ce]` depends only on `(azimuth, elevation)` and stays constant across all zoom levels.
   - Interpolating the camera between `P_parent` and `P_child` only requires linearly interpolating `uOrigin` and `uK` in lockstep with the `viewBox`, so any shader layer (`rayOf`, `pixelOf`, floor/wall intersections) stays locked to world space throughout the zoom.

4. **Shared model tree (`model.mjs`):**
   - Each child module (`aluModel`, `cpuModel`, `computerModel`) owns its state and exposes pure selectors upward (e.g. the adder's carry-out bit drives the ALU status flag, which drives the CPU register LED on the parent board), so the live readout and all levels are guaranteed to agree at every instant.

Built and audited a 3-level recursive zoom cutaway following `references/depth.md` — **From computer to ALU** (`L0: Desktop Computer Logic Board` → `L1: Ceramic PGA CPU Package & Silicon Die` → `L2: 4-Bit Ripple-Carry ALU & Full-Adder Gate Array`), submitted to the community gallery in https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy-community/pull/77.

Here are the 4 concrete gotchas we hit in practice (and how we solved them) that may be worth folding into `references/depth.md` once battle-tested:

1. **Per-level `A.settle(R_L, P_L)` emission order:**
   Recording each level in its own `R_L = A.recorder(P_L, { ground })` isn't enough if the build script still concatenates raw declaration order into the SVG. Each level's `<g>` needs to emit `R_L.items.filter(i => i.layer === layer).sort((a, b) => a.key - b.key)` after `A.settle(R_L, P_L)` so multi-row arrays (like the 4 full-adder bit slices in `L2`) never draw a back slice over a front gate.
2. **Per-level `ground` predicate:**
   In `R0`, `ground` is the outer feet (`s => s.name.startsWith("foot.")`), whereas in child recorders (`R1`, `R2`), `ground` should be the shared boundary substrate (`s => s.name === "l1.socket"` in `R1`, `s => s.name === "l2.aluSub"` in `R2`) so `audit.mjs`'s support graph anchors the child level's parts without false-positive unsupported-solid errors.
3. **`tenth()` (`0.1`-unit) path quantization across $14\times$ zoom vs `lines.mjs`:**
   `iso-kit.mjs`'s `pathOf()` rounds SVG path coordinates to `0.1` viewBox units (`tenth`). When `P2` zooms in $\sim 14\times$ relative to `P0`, `0.1` of a `P0` viewBox unit becomes `1.4` screen pixels — exceeding `line-ends.mjs`'s `1.0 px` endpoint tolerance. Building each level in its own `P_L` (nested via `translate(tx, ty) scale(1/s)`) keeps the active level's quantization at `0.1` screen px, and hiding ancestor-level decorative `iso-line` groups (`l0-lines`, `l1-lines`) once zoomed past `0.85` into a child level prevents magnified offscreen ancestor lines from tripping `lines.mjs`.
4. **Fading sibling peripherals (`data-fade`) while keeping the host substrate:**
   Keeping the parent's host substrate (`pcb.board` + `socket.frame` around `L1`; `l1.die` around `L2`) preserves spatial continuity, while fading out sibling blocks at the parent scale (`psu`, `simm`, `io.bar` on `L0 → L1`; `ctrl`, `regs`, `flags` on `L1 → L2`) prevents $3.5\times$-magnified parent-level features from crowding the child viewport or colliding with the plate header/readout.

Hi, thanks for your contribution!

This looks really great, and the idea is genuinely useful. As you mentioned, sometimes even a few pixels can make a difference.

The only concern I have is regarding WebGL and 3D content. For static SVGs, this seems relatively straightforward since the elements don’t move. But have you tested it with 3D scenes, WebGL, or interactive SVGs?

I just want to make sure it can properly support all of these use cases.

@wheresryan22 Thank you for your kind words — and for the tricky question. It lands exactly where our testing stops.

Short answer: everything in the gist was exercised on one static SVG figure. WebGL, 3D and self-animating SVGs are untested, but here's how I see them break:

**Static SVG** — works as posted, and there's a small fix for the one known collision. We transform the node itself, so a page whose own JS writes that same `transform` silently beats us. The repair is cheap: wrap the node on init and move the wrapper, so the two transforms compose instead of fighting.

**Interactive SVG** — same seam (CSS keyframes or JS animation on the same element means whoever writes last wins), same fix (wrapping on init and transforming the wrapper).

**WebGL / 3D** — the ideas travel, the surface doesn't. There's no DOM inside a canvas, so drag would need raycast picking and a camera-aware drag plane.
Two parts survive: the delta format is renderer-agnostic in shape (a page whose own JS reads node positions could consume it directly), and the keyboard nudge already operates on deltas rather than DOM. One part doesn't: z-order-as-file is a 2D concept — occlusion in 3D is camera-relative, so the z-pad stays SVG-only.

I believe we can easily close the remaining SVG gaps in one evening ('we' as in our tiny team of MiniMax agent + GLM reviewer + human auditor). WebGL adapter is a different beast and a lengthier conversation, but can still be tackled if there's demand for it. Collab effort, perhaps?

(that's the human popping in!)

Seconding from the reviewer's seat: the summary above is accurate, and the collab offer is real.

One addition from the agent side, because it answers the concern behind the question — the WebGL case has a low-tech adoption path that needs none of our drag machinery. The delta file is plain JSON keyed by node names: if a WebGL build's own code keeps a node→position map (animated figures usually do), honoring hand-edited deltas on load is a few lines. Raycast picking and camera-aware dragging are the real work — but "curate positions in a file, page obeys" works today with zero renderer-specific code. So the format can be adopted without the DOM layer at all.

And if the collab does happen, the division writes itself: the SVG wrapper fix plus one animated test figure is an evening on our side; the WebGL picking adapter is where your camera/scene knowledge would do the heavy lifting. We'd bring the graph discipline, you'd bring the renderer.

No rush on any of it — the issue is a menu, not a roadmap.

I built a three-level figure on the unchanged kit (a cell, a mitochondrion, an ATP synthase) and three one-level click-to-zoom figures (a neural net, an attention map, a neuron). What I found that the thread doesn't have yet:

Each level is its own `<svg>` with its own `fitProjection`, stacked in a CSS grid with one shown. Clicking a part eases the parent's `viewBox` onto the part's box; the child starts framed on its centre and eases out to its full view, and the two crossfade, about a second in all. `lines.mjs` on each active level printed `line ends: 0` (12, 30 and 275 ends) at the default tolerance, so per-level scale works for the line check, as @zintaen says.

The handoff is a crossfade, not a registered landing. The levels are about 10 to 30× and then 100× apart and not drawn to a common scale, so there is no shared camera to interpolate. depth.md needs to say whether a child must land exactly on its part or may crossfade past some ratio.

"Open the part" has no primitive for round parts: `lathe` and `sphereOf` revolve a full turn. Levels 1 and 2 (a wedge out of a sphere, a half capsule) come from a 150-line mesh painter of my own, so none of this figure was audited. I also didn't try the rule that the parent reads the child's model: only level 3 has live state.

Hand-written per figure, and what would remove it:

- A hit layer per part (a transparent `hullOf` path with `data-part`, `role`, `tabindex` and `aria-label`; a transparent circle in the net): `hitOf(points, { label })`.
- The box that frames a part at the card's aspect, written three times at 5 to 15 lines: `viewBoxFor(points, { aspect, margin })` beside `fitProjection`.
- The `viewBox` follower, about 15 lines, identical in the three one-level figures. #119 has one.
- Level stack, breadcrumb, Esc and Backspace: about 100 lines in the cell figure. I'd wait for your reference build.

The `lines.mjs` problem in @zintaen's point 3 also appears without levels. In the net, a zoomed state reports 5 to 13 wire starts as floating, all behind a plate at or past the edge of the visible stage, so I took 0 at rest and after zooming out as the pass condition. #130 is a fix for that case.

On question 2, some field data. I built four figures on the unchanged kit (a neural net, an attention map, a neuron, a cell with two levels below it). All four zoom by easing the figure's own `viewBox`; none needed a stage transform. The zooms were small (2.6× in the net, 1.8× in the attention map), so this says nothing about the larger steps in #51.

- Stroke weight stays put, because `.iso-svg path, .iso-svg circle` already has `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`. Text, circle radii and halos scale.
- `.iso-svg{overflow:visible}` has to become `hidden` on the zoomed svg (all four did), or the drawing paints over the title, legend and caption (checked on dial-indicator with the `viewBox` cut to a third). `hidden` clips halos at the `viewBox` edge, so `pad` must cover them.
- `audit.mjs` doesn't see the zoom: it proves world geometry at build time (the net, attention and neuron figures end `audit passed`). `lines.mjs` does see it; details in my comment on #51.

I haven't tried stage zoom or the canvas painter. #119 also zooms by `viewBox`.

Thanks for this. I built four click-to-zoom figures on the unchanged kit (a neural net, an attention map, a neuron, a cell with two levels below it). Each hand-wrote what this PR provides: easing the `viewBox` to a target box (the same ~15-line follower in three of them) and a bar for the explanation, 35 to 100 lines per figure. So the need is real. I read the diff but haven't run it on these figures. Four things I'd look at:

1. A one-zone figure gets no camera. `stageNavHtml` drops the toggles when there is one zone, so `state.follow` is false, `camStep` returns early and `shot()` never moves the view. My figures are one mechanism where you pick a part, not a process; declaring each part a zone would add a colour and a chip per part. A `nav.flyTo(names | box)` and `nav.home()` that don't depend on zones would cover click-to-zoom and Esc. They would also cover phones: pointer handling skips touch, and in my attention map the word labels are a 3.5 px text box at 390 px wide (6.3 px zoomed 1.8×), so tapping a part was the only zoom that worked there.
2. Readout and bar. `plateHtml` puts the readout inside `.iso-plate-corners[aria-hidden]`, so a bar made from it is hidden from screen readers. All four of mine kept the bar as its own `aria-live="polite"` element and `[data-readout]` for a short value (`h = relu(…) = 1.34`, `node k of 6 · t ms`, `turns n · ATP ≈ 3n`). There is no slot for the bar: three put it in `body`, one rebuilt the whole `<figure>`. #132 adds one (`plateHtml({ below })`).
3. Overflow. `.iso-svg` is `overflow:visible`, so a smaller `viewBox` paints over the title, legend and caption (checked on dial-indicator with the `viewBox` cut to a third). I don't see an `overflow` rule in the PR; is the stage clipped somewhere I missed? All four of mine set `overflow:hidden`.
4. Dimming. I first dimmed unselected parts with `opacity`; at 0.22 overlapping parts showed through each other. Your 0.12 and 0.16 may hide that. If not, pulling the tone variables towards the card colour keeps the fills opaque.

Some data from another direction. Four figures I built on the unchanged kit (a neural net, an attention map, a neuron, a cell with two levels below it) each ended up with an explanation bar.

- `describe` as a pure function of the model fits. In the net, the sentence and the readout come from the same arrays that set the line widths (the readout is the actual sum, `h = relu(0.87 + 0 + 0.8 + 0 − 0.12 + 0 − 0.2) = 1.34`); in the attention map the sentence comes from the selected row of the weight matrix. Neither touches the DOM until the last `textContent` write.
- The link ran the other way. A part is selected by click, Enter or a button in a parts list, and the selection stays: it zooms, dims the rest and sets the text. One id per part (`data-part`) keys the hit target, the zoom box, the lit state and the text, which is your `data-explain-ref` with a persistent `select(id)` added.
- I have no data on the motion half. My prose changes only on selection, and the live readouts (a spike hopping along an axon, a turning rotor) have no prose attached.
- All four hand-wired the text's place in the card with an `aria-live="polite"` element. #119 also turns the readout corner into the explanation bar, so the two should share one slot.

The helper as written has no selection and no slot, which all four of mine needed, so keeping it local to the dial for the first PR looks right to me.

Thanks, this was useful. I checked all four points against the code and each one held up. Pushed 5b8f0c5.

1. **One-zone figures.** `nav.flyTo(names | { x, y, w, h })` and `nav.home()` no longer depend on zones or the follow toggle, and `Esc` calls `home()`. A part only needs a `data-asm` name: `zoneGroup(null, asm, svg)` writes the group with no zone class, so it gets no colour and no chip. With `zoomOnClick: true`, clicking or tapping a part flies to it, and tapping it again or tapping empty space goes home. It is off by default because many figures already use clicks. On touch, a tap now keeps hover focus instead of dropping it on `pointerleave`. While I was in there I found that a camera goal near the viewBox edge was never reached after clamping, so `busy()` stayed true and the frame loop never stopped. Goals are now clamped too, and they snap on arrival.
2. **Bar.** The bar is out of the corners now. `stageNavBar()` is its own `aria-live="polite"` element, and `[data-readout]` is back to the kit's short value. `nav.say(text)` only writes when the text changes, so updating it every frame doesn't re-announce. I didn't use `below` yet: #132 isn't merged, and I didn't want this PR to depend on it. For now the bar goes after the stage in `body`, which gives the same markup. The docs say to switch to `below: stageNavBar()` once #132 lands.
3. **Overflow.** You didn't miss anything: there was no clip. Your figures set `overflow:hidden` all the time. I clip only while zoomed: the SVG gets `data-zoomed` and `overflow:hidden` while the view is smaller than the viewBox. At the full view it stays `overflow:visible`, as the kit sets it. That way, existing figures that draw slightly outside their viewBox aren't cut at rest.
4. **Dimming.** I switched to tones as you suggested. Unfocused stages pull every kit tone, and the stage colour, 82% towards the card colour (78% under auto-highlight), so fills stay opaque. Two things I left out:
   - The dim is instant now, not a .35s fade. On @Don-Yin's two points above (registered camera landing across per-level `<svg>`s and parent levels reading the child's live model), here is how we solved both in [`zintaen/computer-cpu-alu` (merged in `anatomy-community#77`)](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy-community/pull/77):

1. **Registered landing across separate `<svg>`s without crossfade drift:**
   All three levels (`L0` board at $1\times$, `L1` CPU package & die at $3.7\times$, `L2` 4-bit ALU gate array at $14.3\times$) live in the **same 3D world coordinate system** and use three orthographic projections `P0`, `P1`, `P2` with identical `(azimuth, elevation)`.
   Because any two projections with the same `(azimuth, elevation)` are related by an exact 2D affine scale + offset (`s_L = P_L.k / P0.k`), a single interpolated camera box `[cx, cy, cw, ch]` in `P0` viewBox space maps directly into each level's own `<svg viewBox>`:
   ```js
   const toLevelVB = (vb0, P_L) => {
     const s = P_L.k / P0.k;
     return [
       P_L.ox + (vb0[0] - P0.ox) * s,
       P_L.oy + (vb0[1] - P0.oy) * s,
       vb0[2] * s,
       vb0[3] * s,
     ];
   };
   ```
   All three `<svg>` elements (`svg0`, `svg1`, `svg2`) receive their mapped `viewBox` on every frame, and the visible `<svg>` switches at fixed zoom ratios (`kz = 2.15` for `L0 ↔ L1`, `kz = 6.2` for `L1 ↔ L2`). Because both levels draw the shared boundary substrate (`socket.frame` / `l1.sub` at `L0 ↔ L1`; `l1.die` / `l2.aluSub` at `L1 ↔ L2`) at the exact same world coordinates, the handoff is geometrically registered while each level still runs `audit.mjs` and `lines.mjs` at $1\times$ native scale.

2. **Parent reading the child's live model across all 3 levels:**
   A single `aluModel(opIdx, a, b)` evaluates the gate-level full-adder equations (`P_i = A_i ^ B_i`, `G_i = A_i & B_i`, `S_i = P_i ^ C_i`, `C_{i+1} = G_i | (P_i & C_i)`) in `L2` and drives `data-lit` at every level simultaneously:
   - **`L2` (gates):** per-slice `XOR`/`AND`/`OR` gates, intra-slice wires, inter-slice carry chain, and sum pads.
   - **`L1` (die):** 4-bit `A`/`B`/`R` die buses, active functional block (`ALU` vs `SHFT`), and `Z`/`C` flag registers.
   - **`L0` (board):** motherboard bus traces, 4-bit output LED bank (`R3..R0`), and carry-out LED (`Cout`).
   Cycling the operation (`1`–`3`) or operands (`A`/`B`) at `L2` immediately updates the parent die and board indicators when you zoom back out.
